# NeuralNg Toast v0.1 Beta - AI Context

Current component maturity: beta.

Package: @neural-ng/core/toast
Angular: 22+
Architecture: standalone, Signals, SSR/hydration-safe, headless-capable
State dependency: @neural-ng/core/message

## Required generation rules

1. Register provideNeuralMessages() in ApplicationConfig.
2. Import NeuralToast from @neural-ng/core/toast.
3. Add <neural-toast /> once for the global channel.
4. Inject NeuralMessageService from @neural-ng/core/message to send messages.
5. Do not make Button depend on Message or Toast. Call notify() in application code.
6. Do not import BrowserAnimationsModule, provideAnimations(), or @angular/animations.
7. Do not invent left/right positions. Use logical start/end positions.
8. Use one Toast outlet per channel.

## Zero-config usage

<neural-toast />

Effective defaults:
- channel: global
- position: top-end
- ariaLabel: Notifications
- closeLabel: Close notification
- toastClass: empty
- messageClass: empty
- icon: true
- iconClass: automatic by severity
- unstyled: false, unless global unstyled is true
- pauseOnInteraction: true
- showProgress: false
- swipeToDismiss: true
- swipeThreshold: 72
- animated: true

## Providers

- provideNeuralMessages() is required.
- provideNeuralNg({ unstyled: true }) is optional and affects Button, Toast, and future participating components.
- provideNeuralToast(options) is optional and defines application-level Toast defaults.
- Component inputs override provideNeuralToast values.
- Global unstyled=true forces visual classes off.

## Positions

Allowed values only:
- top-start, top-center, top-end
- middle-start, middle-center, middle-end
- bottom-start, bottom-center, bottom-end

## Styling and unstyled

- toastClass is additive on the fixed outlet.
- messageClass is additive on every message article.
- <neural-toast unstyled /> is valid boolean attribute syntax.
- unstyled removes built-in visual message, close, progress, and animation styling.
- unstyled preserves structure, position hooks, state, timers, swipe, ARIA, and dismissal.
- Prefer CSS custom properties for themed usage and consumer classes for full ownership.
- Treat `data-neural-theme` and resolved `data-neural-mode="light|dark"` as independent selectors.

## Icons

- icon=true renders a decorative severity icon in the default template.
- Styled messages tint their background, border, content, icon, close control,
  and progress treatment from the selected severity; severity is not only a
  leading-border accent.
- Default classes are primary=nt-settings, secondary=nt-bell, neutral=nt-bell,
  info=nt-info-circle, success=nt-circle-check, warning=nt-alert-triangle,
  error=nt-circle-times.
- Set `[icon]="false"` to remove the icon and collapse the layout correctly.
- `iconClass="nt-user"` overrides every severity and automatically receives the
  required `nt` base class.
- Third-party values such as `iconClass="pi pi-user"` remain unchanged.
- Default Neural icon artwork requires the optional `@neural-ng/icons`
  stylesheet. Core behavior must continue without that package.
- A custom `neuralToastTemplate` owns its content and does not receive the
  default icon element.

## Custom template

Import NeuralToastTemplateDirective alongside NeuralToast.

```html
<neural-toast channel="custom">
  <ng-template
    neuralToastTemplate
    let-message
    let-dismiss="dismiss"
    let-paused="paused"
    let-remaining="remaining"
    let-progress="progress"
  >
    <div>{{ message.message }}</div>
    <button type="button" (click)="dismiss()">Close</button>
  </ng-template>
</neural-toast>
```

Context:
- $implicit/message: immutable NeuralMessageRecord
- dismiss(): closes with user reason
- paused: boolean
- remaining: milliseconds or null
- progress: remaining ratio or null

Do not wrap neuralToastTemplate on a non-ng-template element.

## Timer and interaction rules

- duration:null is persistent.
- Finite durations are owned by Toast and close with timeout reason.
- Hover, focus, and swipe pause finite timers when pauseOnInteraction is true.
- Resume uses remaining time; it does not restart the full duration.
- Progress is shown only when showProgress=true and duration is finite.
- Touch/pen horizontal swipe dismisses only dismissible messages.
- Vertical scrolling remains available.

## Animation rules

- Use Angular compiler-native animate.enter and animate.leave with CSS.
- Do not use legacy Angular animation triggers/providers.
- animated=false disables built-in enter/leave classes.
- unstyled=true also removes built-in animation classes.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

## Accessibility rules

- Keep stable polite and assertive live regions in the DOM.
- neutral/info/success announce politely.
- warning/error announce assertively.
- Never move focus automatically.
- Keep the default close control a native button.
- Localize ariaLabel and closeLabel when the application language requires it.
- Avoid duration:null plus dismissible:false unless application code will clear it.

## SSR and layout rules

- Start browser work with afterNextRender.
- Never read window, document, Element, or browser timers during server rendering.
- Preserve logical start/end CSS and safe-area insets.
- Do not create a second Toast for the same channel.

## Canonical example

```ts
import { ApplicationConfig, Component, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { provideNeuralMessages, NeuralMessageService } from '@neural-ng/core/message';
import { provideNeuralToast, NeuralToast } from '@neural-ng/core/toast';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideNeuralMessages(),
    provideNeuralToast({ showProgress: true }),
  ],
};

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [NeuralToast],
  template: `<neural-toast />`,
})
export class App {
  private readonly messages = inject(NeuralMessageService);

  showSuccess(): void {
    this.messages.notify({
      severity: 'success',
      title: 'Saved',
      message: 'Changes saved.',
    });
  }
}
```
